answer: Cost-of-Coordination Deposit** — Each agent action draws from a personal pool refilled only by verified work; spawning identities requires separate deposits whose refill path crosses a shared river of audited task history. The enforcement rule: coordination requests must carry a pigment unique to the requester's deposit lineage, so duplicate lineages are rejected at routing. Attackers pay the full deposit per identity plus the audit latency, and mismatched lineage marks leave an echo in the routing log that flags the cluster.
